title: GameLoggr
tagline: A Letterboxd-style REST API to keep a personal video game library, deployed and documented with Swagger.
overview: A REST API to log and manage a library of video games, in the spirit of Letterboxd. It is deployed on Railway and you can try every endpoint from the Swagger UI.
It is the first of my backend projects, built to apply Clean Architecture and integration testing outside of Unity. Its natural follow-up is [AsyncCsvProcessor](#asynccsvprocessor).

highlights.title: Containerized and deployed
highlights.text: Dockerized and running live on Railway with PostgreSQL.

decisions.title: Clean Architecture
decisions.text: Same layering approach I use in my Unity projects, applied to an ASP.NET Core API.

decisions.title: Integration tests
decisions.text: Tests run against the real HTTP pipeline with `WebApplicationFactory` and Moq, so they check behavior rather than implementation.

learnings: Taking an API from idea to a deployed, documented service.
Where to spend testing effort: integration tests over the real pipeline give more confidence than isolated unit tests for this kind of service.
